title: Ensure Minimum Password Length is set to 14 or higher
description: Defines the minimum length a password can be. The minimum number of characters of a password that is to be allowed for users or SNMP users. Does not apply to passwords that have already been set. PASS requires min-password-length of 14 or more. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.1 Ensure Minimum Password Length is set to 14 or higher

remediation.command:
set password-controls min-password-length 14
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set the min-password-length setting. CLI:
set password-controls min-password-length 14
GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Password Policy Ensure 'Minimum Password Length' is set to 14 or higher.

title: Ensure Password Complexity is set to 3
description: This checks all new passwords to ensure that they meet basic requirements for strong passwords. The required number of character types are: Upper case alphabetic (A-Z), Lower case alphabetic (a-z), Digits (0-9), Other (everything else). A value of "1" effectively disables this check. Changes to this setting do not affect existing passwords. PASS requires password-controls complexity 3 (or 4). Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.3 Ensure Password Complexity is set to 3

remediation.command:
set password-controls complexity 3
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set the password-controls complexity setting. CLI:
set password-controls complexity 3
GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Password Policy > Password Complexity:
checked the '3 - Require three character types' setting.

title: Ensure Check for Password Reuse is selected and History Length is set to 12 or more
description: Check for reuse of passwords. When a user's password is changed, the new password is checked against the recent passwords for the user. An identical password is not allowed. The number of passwords kept in the record is set by History length. Does not apply to SNMP passwords. Enables or disables password history checking and password history recording, for all users. PASS requires history-checking on and history-length of 12 or more. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.4 Ensure Check for Password Reuse is selected and History Length is set to 12 or more

audit.pattern: (?m)(?:^set password-controls history-checking on[ \t]*$(?s:.*?)^set password-controls history-length (?:1[2-9]|[2-9]\d|[1-9]\d\d+)[ \t]*$|^set password-controls history-length (?:1[2-9]|[2-9]\d|[1-9]\d\d+)[ \t]*$(?s:.*?)^set password-controls history-checking on[ \t]*$)

remediation.command:
set password-controls history-checking on
set password-controls history-length 12
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set tie history-checking setting. CLI:
set password-controls history-checking on
set password-controls history-length 12
GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Password Policy > Password History:
checked the 'Check for Password Reuse' setting.
Navigate to User Management > Password Policy > Password History:
Set 'History Length' is set to 12 or more.

title: Ensure Password Expiration is set to 90 days
description: The number of days for which a password is valid. After that time, the password expires. The count starts when the user changes their passwords. Users are required to change an expired password the next time they log in. If set to never, passwords do not expire. Does not apply to SNMP users. PASS requires password-expiration between 1 and 90 days. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.5 Ensure Password Expiration is set to 90 days

remediation.command:
set password-controls password-expiration 90
save config
# note: the CIS remediation text shows 'history-length 90' by mistake; password-expiration is the setting audited
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set the history-length setting. CLI:
set password-controls history-length 90
GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Password Policy > Mandatory Password Changes:
Password Expiration:
Set 'Password expires after' setting to 90 or less

title: Ensure Warn users before password expiration is set to 7 days
description: The number of days before the password expires that the user starts getting warned they will have to change it. A user that does not log in will not see the warning. PASS requires expiration-warning-days of 7 or less (and not 0). Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.6 Ensure Warn users before password expiration is set to 7 days

remediation.command:
set password-controls expiration-warning-days 7
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set the expiration-warning-days setting. CLI:
set password-controls expiration-warning-days 7
GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Password Policy > Mandatory Password Changes Set 'Warn users before password expiration' is set to 7 days or less.

title: Ensure Lockout users after password expiration is set to 1
description: Lockout users after password expiration. After a user's password has expired, they have this number of days to log in and change it. If they do change their password within that number of days they will be unable to log in: They are locked out. A value of never allows the user to wait as long as they want to change their password. PASS requires expiration-lockout-days 1. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.7 Ensure Lockout users after password expiration is set to 1

remediation.command:
set password-controls expiration-lockout-days 1
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set the expiration-lockout-days setting. CLI:
set password-controls expiration-lockout-days 1
GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Password Policy > Mandatory Password Changes > Lockout users after password expiration:
Checked 'Lockout user after' setting and set to 1 day.

title: Ensure Force users to change password at first login after password was changed from Users page is selected
description: Force users to change password at first login after their password was changed using the command set user password or from the WebUI User Management > Users page. PASS requires force-change-when password. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.10 Ensure Force users to change password at first login after password was changed from Users page is selected

remediation.command:
set password-controls force-change-when password
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set force-change-when setting. CLI:
set password-controls force-change-when password
GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Password Policy > Mandatory Password Change:
Checked the 'Force users to change password at first login after password was changed from Users page' setting.

title: Ensure Deny access after failed login attempts is selected
description: If the configured limit is reached, the user is locked out (unable to log in) for a configurable period of time. PASS requires deny-on-fail enable on. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.11 Ensure Deny access after failed login attempts is selected

remediation.command:
set password-controls deny-on-fail enable on
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set the deny-on-fail setting. CLI:
set password-controls deny-on-fail enable on
GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Password Policy > Deny Access After Failed Login Attempts:
Checked the 'Deny access after failed login attempts' setting.

title: Ensure Maximum number of failed attempts allowed is set to 5 or fewer
description: This only takes effect if Deny access after failed attempts is enabled. The number of failed login attempts that a user is allowed before being locked out. After making that many successive failed attempts, future attempts will fail. When one login attempt succeeds, counting of failed attempts stops, and the count is reset to zero. PASS requires deny-on-fail failures-allowed of 5 or fewer. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.12 Ensure Maximum number of failed attempts allowed is set to 5 or fewer

remediation.command:
set password-controls deny-on-fail failures-allowed 5
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set the deny-on-fail failures-allowed setting. CLI:
set password-controls deny-on-fail failures-allowed 5
GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Password Policy > Deny Access After Failed Login Attempts:
checked and set ' Maximum number of failed attempts allowed is set to' setting to 5 or fewer.

title: Ensure Telnet is disabled
description: Disables the telnet access to the security appliance in the case it has been configured. FAILs if Telnet is enabled (set net-access telnet on). Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.9 Ensure Telnet is disabled

remediation.command:
set net-access telnet off
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to disable the telnet. CLI:
set net-access telnet off
GUI:
Navigate to System Management > Network Access > verify Enable Telnet is unchecked.

title: Ensure Client Authentication is secured.
description: Client Authentication allows a user and device to authenticate to the firewall and inherit pre-configured firewall rules for a set amount of time. By default, these connections are unencrypted yet can travel over unsecured networks. It is recommended that all Client Authentication connections be made using the HTTPS configuration. This both uniquely identifies the gateway and keeps the authentication credentials from being copied when going over the network.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.5.3 Ensure Client Authentication is secured.

audit.command: On the gateway, check $FWDIR/conf/fwauthd.conf in expert mode: the line '259 fwssd in.aclientd wait 259' (Telnet client authentication) must be commented out or absent, and the line '900 fwssd in.ahclientd wait 900' must carry 'ssl:defaultCert' so HTTP client authentication uses HTTPS.

remediation.command:
Comment out or remove the following line from $FWDIR/conf/fwauthd.conf file, or disable the telnet service listening on port 259 by default, write a rule that prevents connections to the daemon in the rulebase.
#259    fwssd       in.aclientd     wait    259
Edit the following line to include SSL setting in $FWDIR/conf/fwauthd.conf file. 900     fwssd       in.ahclientd    wait    900 ssl:defaultCert

title: Ensure Radius or TACACS+ server is configured
description: Configured the TACACS-Servers or Radius server for central authentication. PASS requires a RADIUS or TACACS+ server to be defined. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.5.4 Ensure Radius or TACACS+ server is configured

audit.pattern: (?m)^(?:add aaa radius-servers priority \d+ host \S+|add aaa tacacs-servers priority \d+ server \S+)

remediation.command:
set aaa tacacs-servers state on
add aaa tacacs-servers priority 1 server <IP> key <key> timeout 5
(or) add aaa radius-servers priority 1 host <IP> secret <key> port 1812 timeout 3
save config
# CIS guidance:
run the following command to enable and add TACACS+ servers. CLI:
set aaa tacacs-servers state on
add aaa tacacs-servers priority <priority_value> server
<IP_Address> key <Key> timeout <timeout_value> GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Authentication Servers > TACACS+ configuration > Ensuere Enable TACACS+ authentication is checked
Navigate to User Management > Authentication Servers > TACACS+ configuration > Enable TACACS+ Servers > Add Provide <Server_IP_Address>, <Priority> and <Timeout>. Run the following command to enable and add Radius servers. CLI:
add aaa radius-servers priority <priority_value> host <IP_Address>
secret <Key>  port <Port_number> timeout <timeout_value> GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Authentication Servers > Radius Servers > Add Provide <Server_IP_Address>, <Priority>, <UDP_Port> and <Timeout>.

title: Enable the Firewall Stealth Rule
description: Create a rule to drop Any Service from Any Source or Any VPN that attempts to connect to the gateway.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.1 Enable the Firewall Stealth Rule

audit.command: Login to the Management Server via SmartConsole and create or edit the stealth rule and make sure it is on top of all rules and only allowed sources and services are allowed to access the Gateway.

remediation.command: Login to the Management Server via SmartDashboard and create or edit the stealth rule, allowed only required IP address to manage the gateway and make sure it is on top of all rules.

title: Configure a Default Drop/Cleanup Rule
description: Ensure that the final rule in the rulebase explicitly drops all services, destinations, etc not specifically allowed in the previous rules. It is important that any access not explicitly allowed be explicitly dropped.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.2 Configure a Default Drop/Cleanup Rule

audit.command: Verify the last rule is present in the rulebase which is denying all traffic from any source to any destination.

remediation.command: Create or edit the last rule in the rulebase which is denying all traffic from any source to any destination.

title: Ensure no Allow Rule with Any in Destination filed present in the Firewall Rules
description: The Firewall Rules with Any in Source field allows all the IP Addresses of the Network to access the specified destination configured in the Firewall rules for specific services.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.5 Ensure no Allow Rule with Any in Destination filed present in the Firewall Rules

audit.command: In SmartConsole review the Access Control policy: verify there are no Accept rules with Any in the Destination field. Any such rule must have a documented business justification.

remediation.command: Delete or narrow every Accept rule that has Any in the Destination field.

title: Ensure no Allow Rule with Any in Source filed present in the Firewall Rules
description: The Firewall Rules with Any in the Destination field allows accessing all the IP Addresses of Network from specified Sources configured in the Firewall rules for specific services.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.6 Ensure no Allow Rule with Any in Source filed present in the Firewall Rules

audit.command: In SmartConsole review the Access Control policy: verify there are no Accept rules with Any in the Source field. Any such rule must have a documented business justification.

remediation.command: Delete or narrow every Accept rule that has Any in the Source field.

title: Ensure no Allow Rule with Any in Services filed present in the Firewall Rules
description: The Firewall Rules with Any in the Service field allows accessing all the Services from specified Source to specified Destination configured in the Firewall rules.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.7 Ensure no Allow Rule with Any in Services filed present in the Firewall Rules

audit.command: Verify there are no allowed rules present in the firewall which has Any used in the Service field.

remediation.command: Delete the rule from the firewall which has Any used in the Service field.

title: Ensure Anti-Spoofing is enabled and action is set to Prevent for all Interfaces
description: The Anti-Spoofing is a technique which is used to identify and drop the packets that have a false source IP address. The Anti-Spoofing detect mode is only monitor the Anti-spoofing events while prevent mode drops the Anti-spoofing events.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.12 Ensure Anti-Spoofing is enabled and action is set to Prevent for all Interfaces

audit.command: For all managed gateways verify that Anti-Spoofing is enabled, Anti-Spoofing action is set to Prevent and tracking is set to Log. SmartConsole > Gateways & Servers > select managed Gateway > Network Management > Select each interface > General > Modify - Verify Perform Anti-Spoofing based on Interface topology is checked - Verify Anti-Spoofing action is set to Prevent - Verify Spoof Tracking is set to Log

remediation.command:
For all managed gateways enable the Anti-Spoofing, set the Anti-Spoofing action to Prevent and set the tracking to Log. SmartConsole > Gateways & Servers > select managed Gateway > Network Management > Select each interface > General > Modify
- Checked the Perform Anti-Spoofing based on Interface topology
- Set the Anti-Spoofing action to Prevent
- Set the Spoof Tracking to Log

title: Ensure Disallow Palindromes is selected
description: A palindrome is a sequence of letters, numbers, or characters that can be read the same in each direction. racecar, bob, and noon are some of the famous examples of Palindrome. PASS requires password-controls palindrome-check on. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.2 Ensure Disallow Palindromes is selected

remediation.command:
set password-controls palindrome-check on
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set the palindrome-check setting. CLI:
set password-controls palindrome-check on
GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Password Policy Ensure 'Disallow Palindrome' is checked.

title: Ensure Deny access to unused accounts is selected
description: Deny access to unused accounts. If there has been no successful login attempt in a set period of time, the user is locked out and cannot log in. PASS requires deny-on-nonuse enable on. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.8 Ensure Deny access to unused accounts is selected

remediation.command:
set password-controls deny-on-nonuse enable on
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set the deny-on-nonuse setting. CLI:
set password-controls deny-on-nonuse enable on
GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Password Policy > Deny access to unused accounts:
Checked the 'Deny access to unused accounts' setting.

title: Ensure Days of non-use before lock-out is set to 30
description: Days of non-use before lock-out. The number of days in which a user has not (successfully) logged in before that user is locked out. This only takes effect if Deny access to unused accounts is selected. PASS requires deny-on-nonuse allowed-days of 30 or less. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.9 Ensure Days of non-use before lock-out is set to 30

remediation.command:
set password-controls deny-on-nonuse allowed-days 30
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set the deny-on-nonuse allowed-days setting. CLI:
set password-controls deny-on-nonuse allowed-days 30
GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Password Policy > Deny access to unused accounts:
Set 'Days of non-use before lock-out' to 30 or less. Note: This setting only takes effect if 'Deny access to unused accounts' is enabled.

title: Ensure Allow access again after time is set to 300 or more seconds
description: Allow access again after a user has been locked out (due to failed login attempts). The user is allowed access after the configured time if there have been no login attempts during that time). This setting only takes effect if Deny access after failed login attempts is selected. PASS requires deny-on-fail allow-after of 300 seconds or more. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 1.13 Ensure Allow access again after time is set to 300 or more seconds

remediation.command:
set password-controls deny-on-fail allow-after 300
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set the deny-on-fail allow-afte setting. CLI:
set password-controls deny-on-fail allow-after 300
GUI:
Navigate to User Management > Password Policy > Deny Access After Failed Login Attempts:
Set the 'Allow access again after time' setting to 300 or more seconds.

title: Ensure unused interfaces are disabled
description: Disables the unused interfaces.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.5 Ensure unused interfaces are disabled

audit.command: In clish run 'show interfaces all' (or Network Management > Network Interfaces) and confirm every interface that is not in use has state off ('set interface <if> state off').

remediation.command:
Run the following command disable the unused interface. CLI:
set interface <Interface_Number> state off
GUI:
Navigate to Network Management > Network Interfaces > Open unused Interface > unchecked Enable

title: Ensure IPv6 is disabled if not used
description: Although IPv6 has many advantages over IPv4, not all organizations have IPv6 or dual stack configurations implemented FAILs if IPv6 is enabled (set ipv6-state on); if IPv6 is used, document the exception. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.7 Ensure IPv6 is disabled if not used

remediation.command:
set ipv6-state off
save config
(a restart of the gateway is required for the change to take effect)
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to enable or disable IPv6.
set ipv6-state on
set ipv6-state off

title: Ensure DHCP is disabled
description: Disable the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) server on your device. FAILs if the Gaia DHCP server (or a DHCP subnet) is enabled. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.10 Ensure DHCP is disabled

remediation.command:
set dhcp server disable
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to disable the DHCP. CLI:
set dhcp server disable
GUI:
Navigate to Network Management > DHCP Server > DHCP Server Configuration > veriify Enable DHCP Server is unchecked

title: Ensure SNMP agent is disabled
description: The Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) server is used to listen for SNMP commands from an SNMP management system, execute the commands or collect the information and then send results back to the requesting system. FAILs if the SNMP agent is enabled (set snmp agent on). Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.2.1 Ensure SNMP agent is disabled

remediation.command:
set snmp agent off
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to configure the SNMP. CLI:
set snmp agent off
GUI:
System Management > SNMP > Unhecked the Enable SNMP Agent

title: Ensure SNMP version is set to v3-Only
description: Sets the SNMP v3. PASS requires set snmp agent-version v3-Only. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.2.2 Ensure SNMP version is set to v3-Only

remediation.command:
set snmp agent-version v3-Only
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to configure the SNMP agent-version v3-only CLI:
set snmp agent-version v3-Only
GUI:
Navigate to System Management > SNMP > Select V3-Only in Version

title: Ensure SNMP traps is enabled
description: Enables SNMP traps to be sent to the NMS. PASS requires the authorizationError, coldStart, configurationChange, configurationSave, linkUpLinkDown and lowDiskSpace traps enabled (matched in the alphabetical order clish prints them). Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.2.3 Ensure SNMP traps is enabled

audit.pattern: (?ms)^set snmp traps trap authorizationError enable.*?^set snmp traps trap coldStart enable.*?^set snmp traps trap configurationChange enable.*?^set snmp traps trap configurationSave enable.*?^set snmp traps trap linkUpLinkDown enable.*?^set snmp traps trap lowDiskSpace enable

remediation.command:
set snmp traps trap authorizationError enable
set snmp traps trap coldStart enable
set snmp traps trap configurationChange enable
set snmp traps trap configurationSave enable
set snmp traps trap linkUpLinkDown enable
set snmp traps trap lowDiskSpace enable
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to Configure the SNMP traps. CLI:
set snmp traps trap authorizationError enable
set snmp traps trap coldStart enable
set snmp traps trap configurationChange enable
set snmp traps trap configurationSave enable
set snmp traps trap linkUpLinkDown enable
set snmp traps trap lowDiskSpace enable
GUI:
Navigate to System Management > SNMP > Enabled Traps > Set and select the following traps uthorizationError, coldStart, configurationChange, configurationSave, linkUpLinkDown and lowDiskSpace

title: Ensure SNMP traps receivers is set
description: Enables SNMP traps receivers where traps to be sent to. PASS requires an SNMPv3 trap receiver. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.2.4 Ensure SNMP traps receivers is set

remediation.command:
add snmp traps receiver 10.10.168.86 version v3
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to Configure the SNMP traps receivers. CLI:
add snmp traps receiver 10.10.168.86 version v3
GUI:
Navigate to System Management > SNMP > Trap Receivers Setting > Add > Add IP Address Version details.

title: Ensure NTP is enabled and IP address is set for Primary and Secondary NTP server
description: These settings enable the use of primary and secondary NTP servers to provide redundancy in case of a failure involving the primary NTP server. PASS requires NTP active on with a primary and a secondary server. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.3.1 Ensure NTP is enabled and IP address is set for Primary and Secondary NTP server

audit.pattern: (?m)(?:^set ntp active on[ \t]*$(?s:.*?)^set ntp server primary \S+(?s:.*?)^set ntp server secondary \S+|^set ntp active on[ \t]*$(?s:.*?)^set ntp server secondary \S+(?s:.*?)^set ntp server primary \S+|^set ntp server primary \S+(?s:.*?)^set ntp active on[ \t]*$(?s:.*?)^set ntp server secondary \S+|^set ntp server primary \S+(?s:.*?)^set ntp server secondary \S+(?s:.*?)^set ntp active on[ \t]*$|^set ntp server secondary \S+(?s:.*?)^set ntp active on[ \t]*$(?s:.*?)^set ntp server primary \S+|^set ntp server secondary \S+(?s:.*?)^set ntp server primary \S+(?s:.*?)^set ntp active on[ \t]*$)

remediation.command:
set ntp active on
set ntp server primary <ntp1> version 3
set ntp server secondary <ntp2> version 3
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to enable the NTP and configure the Primary & Secondary NTP server. CLI:
set ntp active on
set ntp server primary ntpserver.time.com version 3
set ntp server primary 10.22.13.33 version 3
GUI:
System Management > Time > Set Time and Date > Checked Set Time and Date automatically using Network Time Protocol (NTP) and configured the Primary NTP Server and Secondary NTP server

title: Ensure CLI session timeout is set to less than or equal to 10 minutes
description: Set the CLI Session Timeout value for device management to 10 minutes or less to automatically close inactive sessions. PASS requires inactivity-timeout between 1 and 10 minutes. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.5.1 Ensure CLI session timeout is set to less than or equal to 10 minutes

remediation.command:
set inactivity-timeout 10
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to Configure the Inactivity Timeout for Command Line. CLI:
set inactivity-timeout 10
GUI:
Navigate to System Management > Session > Command Line Shell  >  Inactivity Timeout - Set to 10 or less

title: Ensure Web session timeout is set to less than or equal to 10 minutes
description: Set the WebUI Session Timeout value for device management to 10 minutes or less to automatically close inactive sessions. PASS requires web session-timeout between 1 and 10 minutes. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.5.2 Ensure Web session timeout is set to less than or equal to 10 minutes

remediation.command:

title: Ensure allowed-client is set to those necessary for device management
description: Permit only the necessary IP addresses to be used to manage the device. FAILs if allowed-client still permits any host. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).

add allowed-client network ipv4-address <mgmt-net> mask-length 24
delete allowed-client host any-host

delete allowed-client host (ipv4-address | ipv6-address) <IP

Navigate to System Management > Host Access > Allowed Hosts > Select and Delete the not required IP address or Network

set syslog mgmtauditlogs on
save config

Run the following command to enable the mgmtauditlogs. CLI:
set syslog mgmtauditlogs on
GUI:
Navigate to System Management > System Logging > System Logging checked the Send audit logs to management server upon successful configuration

title: Logging should be enable for all Firewall Rules
description: The Track Field defines how the events of the rule are captured.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.8 Logging should be enable for all Firewall Rules

audit.command: Verify all Track field in all firewall rules should have set to Log.

remediation.command: Set the Track field to Log in all firewall rules.

title: Review and Log Implied Rules
description: Rulebase clarity helps all workers and reviewers. Stating rules explicitly in the rulebase makes policy analysis and review significantly easier. Select the ‗Log Implied Rules‘ to ensure all understand when connectivity is denied or allowed through a subtle Implied Rule.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.9 Review and Log Implied Rules

audit.command: Go to the following path in the Smart Console and verify Log Implied Rules is enabled. Navigate to Global Properties > Firewall Verify Log Implied Rules is enabled

remediation.command:
Go to the following path in the Smart Console and enabled the Log Implied Rules.
Navigate to Global Properties > Firewall Enable the Log Implied Rules

title: Ensure Drop Out of State TCP Packets is enabled
description: The Drop out of state TCP Packets setting will drop the out of state or non-synchronized TCP Packets for which firewall does not have a matching state table entry.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.10 Ensure Drop Out of State TCP Packets is enabled

audit.command: Go to the following path and verify Drop Out of State TCP Packets and Log on Drop is enabled. SmartConsole > Global Properties > Stateful Inspection Verify Drop Out of State TCP Packets and Log on Drop is checked.

remediation.command: Go to the following path and checked the Drop Out of State TCP Packets and Log on Drop. SmartConsole > Global Properties > Stateful Inspection Checked the Drop Out of State TCP Packets and Log on Drop

title: Ensure Drop Out of State ICMP Packets is enabled
description: This drops the out of state ICMP packets.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.11 Ensure Drop Out of State ICMP Packets is enabled

audit.command: Go to the following path and verify Drop Out of State ICMP Packets and Log on Drop is enabled. SmartConsole > Global Properties > Stateful Inspection Verify Drop Out of State ICMP Packets and Log on Drop is checked.

remediation.command: Go to the following path and checked the Drop Out of State ICMP Packets and Log on Drop. SmartConsole > Global Properties > Stateful Inspection Checked the Drop Out of State ICMP Packets and Log on Drop

title: Ensure Accept RIP is not enabled
description: The Accept RIP is a Global property setting which you can set either to accept or reject the RIP packets which is using UDP Port 520. RIP maintains information about reachable systems and routes to those systems.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.14 Ensure Accept RIP is not enabled

audit.command: Verify Accept RIP under Global Properties is not enabled. SmartConsole > Gateways & Servers > select each Gateway > Firewall Veiry Accept RIP is unchecked.

remediation.command: Go to the following path and Configured the Accept RIP. SmartConsole > Gateways & Servers > select each Gateway > Firewall Unchecked the Accept RIP

title: Ensure Accept Domain Name over TCP (Zone Transfer) is not enabled
description: The 'Domain Name Over TCP (Zone transfer)' is a global property setting which is used to allow or reject all the TCP-type DNS packets to and from anywhere. These rules are considered as rule zero which are executed before any user-defined rules.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.15 Ensure Accept Domain Name over TCP (Zone Transfer) is not enabled

audit.command: Verify Accept Accept Domain Name over TCP (Zone Transfer) under Global Properties is not enabled. SmartConsole > Gateways & Servers > select each Gateway > Firewall Veiry Accept Accept Domain Name over TCP (Zone Transfer) is unchecked.

remediation.command: Go to the following path and Configured the Accept Accept Domain Name over TCP (Zone Transfer). SmartConsole > Gateways & Servers > select each Gateway > Firewall Unchecked the Accept Accept Domain Name over TCP (Zone Transfer)

title: Ensure Accept Domain Name over UDP (Queries) is not enabled
description: The 'Domain Name Over UDP (Queries)' is a global property setting which is used to allow or reject all the UDP-type DNS packets to and from anywhere. These rules are considered as rule zero which are execute before any user-defined rules.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.16 Ensure Accept Domain Name over UDP (Queries) is not enabled

audit.command: Verify Accept Accept Domain Name over UDP (Queries) under Global Properties is not enabled. SmartConsole > Gateways & Servers > select each Gateway > Firewall Verify Accept Accept Domain Name over UDP (Queries) is unchecked.

remediation.command: Go to the following path and Configured the Accept Accept Domain Name over UDP (Queries). SmartConsole > Gateways & Servers > select each Gateway > Firewall Unchecked the Accept Accept Domain Name over UDP (Queries)

title: Ensure Accept ICMP Requests is not enabled
description: The 'Accept ICMP requests' is a global property setting which is used to allow the ICMP requests from any location. ICMP is used to send control messages (for example, ping, destination unreachable, source quench, route change) to other systems. These rules are considered as rule zero which are executed before any user-defined rules.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.17 Ensure Accept ICMP Requests is not enabled

audit.command: Verify Accept Accept ICMP Requests under Global Properties is not enabled. SmartConsole > Gateways & Servers > select each Gateway > Firewall Verify Accept Accept ICMP Requests is unchecked.

remediation.command: Go to the following path and Configured the Accept Accept ICMP Requests. SmartConsole > Gateways & Servers > select each Gateway > Firewall Unchecked the Accept Accept ICMP Requests

title: Ensure Allow bi-directional NAT is enabled
description: Allow bi-directional NAT applies to automatic NAT rules in the NAT Rule Base and allows two automatic NAT rules to match a connection. Without Bidirectional NAT, only one automatic NAT rule can match a connection.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.18 Ensure Allow bi-directional NAT is enabled

audit.command: Verify Allow bi-directional NAT under Global Properties is enabled. SmartConsole > Gateways & Servers > select each Gateway > NAT - Network Address Translation Verify Allow bi-directional NAT is checked.

remediation.command: SmartConsole > Gateways & Servers > select each Gateway > NAT - Network Address Translation: check Allow bi-directional NAT (the CIS text says 'Unchecked', which contradicts the recommendation).

title: Ensure Automatic ARP Configuration NAT is enabled
description: Proxy ARP is a mechanism that allows the configuration of a Gateway to respond to ARP requests on behalf of other hosts.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.19 Ensure Automatic ARP Configuration NAT is enabled

audit.command: Verify Automatic ARP Configuration NAT under Global Properties is enabled. SmartConsole > Gateways & Servers > select each Gateway > NAT - Network Address Translation Verify Automatic ARP Configuration NAT is checked.

remediation.command: SmartConsole > Gateways & Servers > select each Gateway > NAT - Network Address Translation: check Automatic ARP Configuration (the CIS text says 'Unchecked', which contradicts the recommendation).

title: Ensure Logging is enabled for Track Options of Global Properties
description: This defines the system-wide logging and alerting of parameters.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 3.20 Ensure Logging is enabled for Track Options of Global Properties

audit.command: Verify Logging is set to Log or Popup Alert or Mail Alert or SNMP Trap Alert for the following events SmartConsole > Global Properties > Log and Alert > Track Options VPN successful key exchange VPN packet handling errors VPN configuration & key exchange errors IP Options drop Administrative Notification Connection matched by SAM Dynamic object resolution failure Packet is incorrectly tagged Packet tagging brute force attack Verify Log every authenticated HTTP connection is enabled.

remediation.command: SmartConsole > Global Properties > Log and Alert > Track Options: set Log (or Popup Alert, Mail Alert or SNMP Trap Alert) for VPN successful key exchange, VPN packet handling errors, VPN configuration & key exchange errors, IP Options drop, Administrative Notification, Connection matched by SAM, Dynamic object resolution failure, Packet is incorrectly tagged and Packet tagging brute force attack. Check Log every authenticated HTTP connection.

title: Ensure the admin user shell is clish
description: Giving admin the Expert bash shell by default bypasses clish role controls. PASS requires 'set user admin shell /etc/cli.sh'. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark - User Management - Admin shell (verify section number for your Gaia release)

remediation.command:
set user admin shell /etc/cli.sh
save config
WebUI: User Management > Users > admin > Shell = /etc/cli.sh.

title: Ensure logs are sent to a remote syslog server
description: PASS requires at least one 'add syslog log-remote-address' entry. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output.

remediation.command:
add syslog log-remote-address 10.0.0.50 level info
save config

title: Ensure 'Login Banner' is set
description: Configure a login banner, ideally approved by the organization's legal team. This banner should, at minimum, prohibit unauthorized access, provide notice of logging or monitoring, and avoid using the word "welcome" or similar words of invitation. PASS requires set message banner on (with an organisation-defined msgvalue). Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).

save config

set message banner on msgvalue "Organization_Banner"

title: Ensure 'Message Of The Day (MOTD)' is set
description: Sets the MOTD message. PASS requires set message motd on (with an organisation-defined msgvalue). Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).

title: Ensure Core Dump is enabled
description: A Core Dump contains the recorded state of the working memory and CPU's contents of the Gaia system at the time that a Gaia process terminated abnormally. The core file is stored in the /var/log/dump/usermode directory. PASS requires set core-dump enable. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.3 Ensure Core Dump is enabled

remediation.command:
set core-dump enable
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set Core Dump.
set core-dump enable
GUI:
Navigate to System Management > Core Dump > select Enable Core Dumps

title: Ensure Config-state is saved
description: The 'Config state' setting provides the detail of the current configuration which is saved or unsaved. Saved state indicates the current configuration of the system is matched with the saved configuration, while unsaved state indicates a configuration change has been made and it has not been saved to the configuration file.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.4 Ensure Config-state is saved

audit.command: In clish run 'show config-state'; it must report 'saved'. If it reports 'unsaved', review the pending change and run 'save config'.

remediation.command:
Run the following command to save the configuration.
save config

title: Ensure DNS server is configured
description: Gaia uses the Domain Name Service (DNS) to translate host names into IP addresses. To enable DNS lookups, you must specify the primary DNS server for your system. You can also specify secondary and tertiary DNS servers. When resolving host names, the system consults the primary name server. If a failure or time-out occurs, the system consults the secondary name server, and if necessary, the tertiary. PASS requires a primary DNS server (add secondary and tertiary as well). Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.1.6 Ensure DNS server is configured

remediation.command:
set dns primary <IP>
set dns secondary <IP>
set dns tertiary <IP>
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set DNS server. CLI:
set dns primary <IP_Address>
set dns secondary <IP_Address>
set dns tertiary <IP_Address>
GUI:
Navigate to Network Management > Hosts and DNS > DNS Set Primary, secondary and tertiary DNS server address.

title: Ensure Host Name is set
description: Changes the device default hostname. PASS requires a hostname to be set. Audited against the Gaia clish 'show configuration' output (run 'show configuration' in clish on each gateway and management server and save the full output).

set hostname <name>
save config
# CIS guidance:
Run the following command to set Host Name. CLI:
set hostname <name>
GUI:

title: Ensure timezone is properly configured
description: Sets the local time zone information so that the time displayed by the device is more relevant to those who are viewing it.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.3.2 Ensure timezone is properly configured

audit.command: In clish run 'show timezone' (System Management > Time) and confirm the time zone matches the organisation's standard (for example Etc/UTC).

remediation.command:
Run the following command to Configure the Timezone used by the enterprise (GMT, UTC, EDT, PST). CLI:
set timezone Asia / Kolkata
GUI:
System Management > Time > Set Time Zone > Time Zone

title: Ensure 'System Backup' is set.
description: List last-successful backup which is taken either locally or on a remote server. The backup can be taken locally on the device and also on a remote server via FTP, tftp or scp. The backup which is taken last is marked with (latest) in backup type.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.4.1 Ensure 'System Backup' is set.

audit.command: In clish run 'show backup last-successful' (Maintenance > System Backup) and confirm a recent successful backup exists, stored locally or on an SCP/FTP/TFTP server.

remediation.command:
Run the following command to Configure the backup. CLI:
To take the backup local on the device.
add backup local
To take the backup of FTP or SCP server.
add backup [ftp|scp] ip [IP Address] path [Path to store backup]
username [Username] password [Password]
To take the backup on tftp server.
add backup tftp [IP address of tftp server]
GUI:
Navigate to Maintenance > System Backup  >  Backup > Select (This appliance | SCP Server | FTP Server | TFTP Server)

title: Ensure 'Snapshot' is set
description: An image of the system partition creates when takes the snapshots, includes all the configuration settings, Operating System and Checkpoint files. The locally stored firewall logs are not stored in the snapshots, as log partition is not included in the Snapshots. Snapshots can be restored on the same hardware on which it takes or on the same configuration hardware.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.4.2 Ensure 'Snapshot' is set

audit.command: In clish run 'show snapshots' (Maintenance > Snapshot Management) and confirm at least one current snapshot (restore point) exists.

remediation.command:
Run the following command to take the snapshot. CLI:
To take the snapshot run the following command on the device.
add snapshot [snapshot_name]
GUI:
Navigate to Maintenance > Snapshot Management > New Provide the Name and description for the snapshot

title: Configuring Scheduled Backups
description: The backup can be scheduled to take daily, weekly or monthly. The backup can be taken locally on the device and also on a remote server via FTP, tftp or scp. The backup which is taken last is marked with (latest) in backup type.
reference: CIS Check Point Firewall Benchmark v1.1.0 - 2.4.3 Configuring Scheduled Backups

audit.command: GUI: Navigate to Maintenance > System Backup > Scheduled Backup

remediation.command:
GUI:
Navigate to Maintenance > System Backup > Scheduled Backup > Add Scheduled Backup Provide the Backup Type and Backup Schedule as per organization's policy.
